nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ni(OH)2/NF
nodes.procedure: 1 mmol NiCl2·6H2O (0.2377 g), 6 mmol NH4F (0.2222 g), and 12 mmol CH4N2O (0.7207 g) were blended with 50 mL H2O and agitated for 30 min. The solution was transferred to a 50 mL polytetrafluoroethylene autoclave liner containing NF (2 × 4 cm²), maintained at 120 °C for 6 h, rinsed with deionized water several times after cooling, and dried for 24 h under vacuum condition of 60 °C to obtain Ni(OH)2/NF.

nodes.name: Pulsed electrodeposition of P-Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO/NF
nodes.procedure: Pulsed electrodeposition method was used to prepare P-Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO/NF. The working electrode was Ni(OH)2-NiO/NF, the reference electrode was Hg2Cl2 and the Counter electrode was Pt in the electrolyte consisting of 10 mM PdCl2, 0.5 M H3BO3, and 1 M NaCl. The electrochemical parameters were: -0.01 A (5 s); –0.001 A (1 s); 100 cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Ni(OH)2-NiO with sheet-like morphology and spike-like Pd morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The microstructures of Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and Ni(OH)2-NiO was sheet-like while Pd was spike-like (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals spike-like Pd composed of Pd nanoparticles facilitating mass transfer and exposing active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images revealed that the spike-like Pd was composed of Pd nanoparticles, which not only facilitated efficient mass transfer but also exposed a greater number of active sites (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows three-phase interface with lattice spacings of 0.225 nm (Pd 111), 0.233 nm (β-Ni(OH)2 101), 0.209 nm (NiO 200).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image provided further confirmation of the crystalline of Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO... with highlighted lattice spacings of 0.225 nm, 0.233 nm, and 0.209 nm corresponding to the (111), (101), and (200) planes of Pd, β-Ni(OH)2, and NiO respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Ni 2p peaks shift negatively and Pd 3d peaks shift positively by ~0.3 eV in Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO compared to individual components, confirming significant electronic interaction and electron transfer from Pd to Ni(OH)2-NiO support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon loading the substrate with Pd, the peaks of Pd 3d in Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO shifted towards higher binding energy (≈0.3 eV) compared with Pd (Fig. 1f), and the peaks of Ni 2p in Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO shifted towards lower binding energy (≈0.3 eV) compared with Ni(OH)2-NiO (Fig. 1g), confirming a significant electronic interaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS valence band spectra show d-band center of Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO/NF shifts up by ~0.33 eV to -3.00 eV compared to Pd/NF at -3.33 eV; calculated d-band centers are -1.63 eV and -1.76 eV respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S5a, the d-band center of the Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO/NF was observed to shift up by ~0.33 eV compared to that of Pd/NF (-3.33 eV)... the calculated d-band center for Pd@Ni(OH)2-NiO/NF and Pd/NF were determined to be -1.63 eV and -1.76 eV (Figure S36).
